newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria repeats rejection of Israeli peace proposal.
newsitem.headline: Syria repeats rejection of Israeli peace proposal.

text.p: Syria reiterated its rejection on Saturday of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal to resume peace talks, saying it did not contain a commitment to trading land for peace.

The official Syrian newspaper al-Thawra also criticised the United States for supporting the Israeli proposal and urged a united Arab stand to face the "dangerous alternatives resulting from the failure of Netanyahu's plan".
"To continue misleading the world and America he (Netanyahu) tried in his latest visit to use new ways to propose the idea... saying that there is a draft plan to resume the talks," al-Thawra said.
"This draft is based on a strange set up, words and understandings. and what is strange is that the U.S. agrees and tries to market it as if it had nothing to do with the peace process," it said.

Washington announced earlier in the week that Israel and the United States, sponsor of the peace process which opened in Madrid in 1991, had new proposals to restart the Syrian-Israeli peace negotiations.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara on Thursday said Syria would not accept new formulas unless they are based on the agreements reached with Israel's Labour government voted from office in May.
Washington denied on Friday that Damascus rejected the offer and said both sides were discussing the proposal put forward following a visit to the United States this week by Netanyahu.
